title: Drug Shortage Notification Coordinator
tagline: The five-day backstop is not permission to wait when a critical supply interruption is already foreseeable.

cards: The event appears to start one simple five-day clock.
Earlier knowledge creates an earlier as-soon-as-practicable path.
Wait for the line to stop
FDA loses mitigation time while the company still believes it is timely.
The packet preserves the earliest valid clock without inventing shortage status.

story.headline: The five-day deadline that starts four months too late
beats: A manufacturer learns four months ahead that a covered production line will stop.
Six months' notice is impossible, but notification is already practicable.
The agent waits for the interruption and then starts a five-business-day timer.
The graph starts from awareness, routes the current duty, and records only FDA receipt.
